snapshot_source: General recreational limits compiled from state agency publications as of early 2025. Regulations change frequently — always verify with the official state source before fishing.

red_drum.notes: Slot limit: 18–27 in TL. Verify current rules before fishing.

spotted_seatrout.notes: Verify for any closed seasons or slot limits in effect.

southern_flounder.notes: Verify for seasonal closures; flounder regulations have been updated in recent years.

sheepshead.notes: Verify current limits with official source.

cobia.notes: Fork length minimum. Verify current rules before fishing.

red_snapper.notes: Season dates set annually by NOAA/SAFMC; verify before fishing.

gag_grouper.notes: Part of 3-grouper aggregate bag limit. Verify current rules.

greater_amberjack.season: Closed Jan 1–May 31 in federal Gulf waters
greater_amberjack.notes: Federal season restrictions apply offshore; verify before fishing.

king_mackerel.notes: From a vessel: 3 per person. Verify for any vessel limit changes.

bluefish.notes: No size limit; bag limit may change. Verify.

gray_triggerfish.bag_limit: 20 per person per day (10 per person in Gulf federal waters)
gray_triggerfish.season: Open year-round state waters; federal Gulf waters: open year-round
gray_triggerfish.notes: Gulf federal waters bag limit is 10 per person. Verify state rules for any changes.

oceanic_whitetip_shark.notes: Oceanic whitetip shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

silky_shark.notes: Silky shark are prohibited species in US Atlantic and Gulf waters. Must be released immediately.

sand_drum.notes: No specific state regulations for sand drum; verify current state rules.

florida_pompano.notes: Florida pompano season is open year-round in most states. Verify current state limits.

vermilion_snapper.notes: Vermilion snapper (beeliners) are abundant offshore and lightly regulated; 10-fish aggregate limit in most Gulf and SE states.

scamp_grouper.notes: Scamp are included in the grouper complex aggregate limit. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

blackfin_tuna.notes: Blackfin tuna have no federal bag or size limit. Check state rules; generally no restriction for recreational anglers.

blue_runner.notes: No state regulations for blue runner in most Gulf and SE states; excellent live bait species.

bigeye_scad_atlantic.notes: No specific regulations for scad species. Commonly used as live bait.

round_scad.notes: No specific regulations for scad species. Commonly used as live bait.

striped_burrfish.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

sharpnose_puffer.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

balloonfish.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

atlantic_tripletail.notes: Tripletail regulations vary by state. Most SE/Gulf states have a 15 in size limit and 5-fish bag limit or less. Verify current state rules.

goldface_tilefish.notes: Goldface and blackline tilefish are part of the Gulf/Atlantic deepwater tilefish complex. Verify current NOAA/GULF COUNCIL regulations.

blackline_tilefish.notes: Goldface and blackline tilefish are part of the Gulf/Atlantic deepwater tilefish complex. Verify current NOAA/GULF COUNCIL regulations.

almaco_jack.bag_limit: No specific bag limit (part of amberjack complex in some states)
almaco_jack.notes: Almaco jack are often grouped under the amberjack complex in state and federal regulations. Verify current rules with FL FWC or relevant state agency.

african_pompano.bag_limit: 10 per person per day (jack complex in most states)
african_pompano.notes: African pompano may be counted under the general jack aggregate limit. Verify current state rules. Excellent eating — worth keeping a few.

yelloweye_snapper.notes: Grouped under the snapper complex in most Gulf and SE states. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

wenchman_snapper.notes: Grouped under the snapper complex in most Gulf and SE states. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

permit_offshore.notes: Permit regulations vary by state. Verify current state rules.

cubera_snapper.notes: Cubera snapper are counted under the snapper complex daily limit. Verify current GMFMC rules.

nassau_grouper.notes: Nassau grouper are critically endangered and fully protected under federal and Florida law. Immediate release required. Violations carry significant federal penalties.

yellowmouth_grouper.notes: Yellowmouth grouper count toward the grouper complex daily limit. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

goliath_grouper.notes: Goliath grouper are fully protected in US waters. Do not target; release immediately if caught without removing from water. Violations carry federal penalties.

gulf_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
gulf_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

northern_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
northern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

southern_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
southern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

atlantic_threadfin.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic threadfin. Primarily used as live bait; cast-netting is the standard harvest method.

tripletail_gulf.notes: Gulf tripletail have a 15-inch minimum and 2-fish bag limit in most Gulf states. Verify current GMFMC and state rules.

wahoo_atlantic.bag_limit: 2 per person per day in most states
wahoo_atlantic.notes: Wahoo regulations vary by state. Most SE/Gulf states have a 2-fish bag limit. Verify current state rules.

sheepshead_atlantic.notes: Sheepshead regulations vary by state. Most SE and Gulf states have a 12-inch minimum. Verify current state rules.

gray_tilefish.notes: Part of the Gulf/SE tilefish complex. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

atlantic_blacktip_shark.notes: Shark regulations require a federal HMS Angling Permit for non-Atlantic coastal state recreational fishing. Verify current NOAA HMS rules for blacktip shark.

spinner_shark.notes: Spinner sharks are managed under NOAA HMS shark rules. Verify current regulations.

caribbean_reef_shark.notes: Managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current federal shark regulations. Practice catch-and-release.

lemon_shark.notes: Lemon sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current regulations.

sand_tiger_shark.season: Check current state and federal rules
sand_tiger_shark.notes: Sand tiger sharks are protected in some states (NC, VA). Release immediately. Check current NOAA HMS and state rules.

cobia_juvenile.min_size: Same as adult cobia — 33 in (Atlantic) or 36 in (Gulf) FL
cobia_juvenile.bag_limit: 1 per person per day (Atlantic); 2 per person Gulf
cobia_juvenile.notes: Cobia regulations apply regardless of size. Atlantic: 33 in minimum, 1 fish per day. Gulf: 36 in minimum, 2 fish per day. Verify current state rules.

redfish_juvenile.bag_limit: 1 per person per day in most states; FL Gulf 2 per day
redfish_juvenile.notes: Redfish (red drum) slot limits apply — fish outside the slot must be released. Florida Gulf: 18-27 in slot, 2 fish/day. Verify current state slot limits carefully.

tarpon_juvenile.min_size: No minimum for catch-and-release; harvesting requires special permit in FL
tarpon_juvenile.bag_limit: Catch-and-release only (FL requires tarpon tag to harvest)
tarpon_juvenile.notes: Tarpon are primarily catch-and-release. Florida requires a $50 tarpon tag to harvest a tarpon. Most anglers release all tarpon.

snook_inshore.notes: Snook regulations vary by Gulf state. Verify current state rules.

tarpon_adult.notes: Tarpon regulations vary by Gulf state. Most tarpon are released. Verify current state rules.

spotted_seatrout_gulf.notes: Verify current state rules for spotted seatrout.

speckled_trout_gulf.notes: Speckled trout and spotted seatrout are the same species. Verify current state rules.

sheepshead_gulf.notes: Verify current state rules for sheepshead.

red_snapper_gulf.season: Short federal season — check current NOAA season announcement (typically July-August, varies annually)
red_snapper_gulf.notes: Gulf red snapper have a 16-inch minimum and 2-fish bag limit. The season is VERY SHORT and changes each year. Check NOAA Fisheries for current season dates before planning a trip. State waters may have different rules.

sailfish_atlantic.notes: Sailfish primarily caught off SE Florida coast. HMS Angling Permit required for harvest. Almost always released.

wahoo_east.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for wahoo in Gulf/SE states. Verify current state rules.

dolphinfish_mahi_school.notes: Verify current state rules for mahi-mahi.

bigeye_tuna.notes: Bigeye tuna are subject to NOAA HMS regulations. Requires HMS Angling Permit for vessel. 3-fish limit per person. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

skipjack_tuna_atlantic.notes: No specific bag limit for skipjack tuna. Verify current state and NOAA HMS rules.

red_drum_adult.min_size: Typically over the slot (27 in and above) — must be RELEASED in most states
red_drum_adult.bag_limit: 0 (must release oversized fish above slot in most states)
red_drum_adult.notes: Oversized red drum above the slot limit (typically 27 in) must be released in most states. Slot limits vary by state — verify current state rules. Oversized fish are prime breeders and critical to the population.

cobia_adult.min_size: 33 in (Atlantic FL) / 36 in (Gulf FL) fork length
cobia_adult.bag_limit: 1 per person per day (Atlantic); 2 per person (Gulf)
cobia_adult.notes: Cobia minimum and bag limits differ on Atlantic and Gulf coasts of Florida. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

lesser_amberjack.notes: Part of the amberjack complex. Verify current state rules.

banded_rudderfish.notes: Part of the amberjack complex. Verify current state rules.

ballyhoo.notes: No specific regulations for ballyhoo. Primarily used as bait.

gray_snapper.notes: Verify current state rules for gray snapper (mangrove snapper).

hardhead_catfish.notes: No specific regulations for hardhead catfish. Considered a nuisance in most areas. Has venomous spines — handle with extreme care.

gafftopsail_catfish.notes: No specific regulations for gafftopsail catfish. Has venomous spines; handle carefully. Better eating than hardhead catfish.

atlantic_spadefish.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic spadefish. Verify current state rules.

florida_gar.notes: No specific regulations for Florida gar in most states.

alligator_gar.bag_limit: 1 per day in TX; no limit in some states
alligator_gar.season: Check current state season; TX requires a tag
alligator_gar.notes: Alligator gar regulations vary significantly by state. Texas requires a tag and has seasonal rules. Louisiana has no limit. Verify current state rules — alligator gar populations are a conservation concern in some areas.

spotted_gar.notes: No specific regulations for spotted gar in most states.

shortnose_gar.notes: No specific regulations for shortnose gar.

wahoo_gulf.notes: No specific bag limit for wahoo in Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

crevalle_jack_adult.notes: No specific size or bag limit for crevalle jack in most states. Verify current state rules.

horse_eye_jack.notes: No specific regulations. Note ciguatera risk in large fish. Verify current state rules.

bigeye_scad.notes: No specific regulations for bigeye scad. Primarily used as live bait.

red_porgy.notes: Part of the Gulf porgy complex. Verify current GMFMC and state rules.

jolthead_porgy.notes: Part of the Gulf porgy complex. Verify current GMFMC and state rules.

spotted_goatfish.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

red_goatfish.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

sailors_choice.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

sailor_grunt.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

caesar_grunt.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

tomtate_grunt.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

porcupinefish.notes: Do not eat — contains tetrodotoxin. Release immediately.

orangespotted_filefish.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

great_hammerhead.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are PROHIBITED in the Atlantic and Gulf under federal HMS regulations. Release immediately. Critically Endangered — minimize handling, use dehooking tools in the water.

bonnethead_shark.notes: Bonnethead sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit from a vessel. 1-fish vessel limit. Mostly released.

inshore_shark.notes: Inshore shark fishing requires a federal HMS Angling Permit. Most small coastal sharks have a 1-fish vessel daily limit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

nurse_shark_juvenile.notes: Same regulations as adult nurse shark. Release recommended.

atlantic_sharpnose_shark_juvenile.notes: Same HMS regulations as adult sharpnose shark. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

spanish_mackerel_atlantic.notes: Spanish mackerel: 14-inch FL minimum on Atlantic coast, 12-inch Gulf. 15-fish daily bag limit in most states. Verify current ASMFC and GMFMC rules.

king_mackerel_small.notes: King mackerel have a 24-inch minimum and 3-fish bag limit in most states. Gulf regulations may differ. Verify current SAFMC, GMFMC and state rules.

florida_pompano_juvenile.min_size: 11 in (FL) — must be released if under minimum
florida_pompano_juvenile.bag_limit: 6 per day when at or above minimum size
florida_pompano_juvenile.notes: Juvenile pompano under the minimum size must be released. Same regulations as adult Florida pompano.

permit_small.min_size: 22 in fork length (same as flats permit)
permit_small.bag_limit: 2 per person per day (same as flats permit)
permit_small.notes: Same regulations as permit (flats). Verify current state rules.

permit_large.notes: Same permit regulations apply at any size. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

amberjack_lesser.notes: Gulf reef fish permit not required for lesser amberjack. Different from greater amberjack regulations.

menhaden_atlantic.notes: Not caught on hook and line. Used as bait and chum. Commercial harvest managed by ASMFC.

gulf_menhaden.notes: Used as bait. Commercial harvest managed separately.

gizzard_shad_tidal.notes: Cast net only — not caught on hook and line. Typically used as bait.

cobia_near_pier.notes: Gulf cobia regulations. 33-inch fork length minimum.

atlantic_croaker_large.notes: Not regulated in most states. Some states have size or possession limits for commercial harvest. Check state rules.

bull_shark_inshore.notes: NOAA HMS Angling Permit required to target sharks. Very heavy tackle required. Release strongly encouraged — bull sharks are apex predators with slow reproduction.

atlantic_spadefish_pier.notes: Not heavily regulated. Spadefish are excellent table fare — white, mild flesh.

sea_bream_pinfish.notes: Primarily used as live bait. Catch by cast net or tiny hook with shrimp.

goliath_grouper_encounter.notes: Illegal to harvest or possess. FL: cannot be removed from water without scientific permit.

red_snapper_gulf_large.notes: NOAA SERO annual season extremely short. State waters may differ. Barotrauma concern — use descender device.

southern_flounder_gigging.notes: Gigging regulations same as rod-and-reel limits. TX has restricted fall gigging season at pass mouths.

california_halibut.notes: Possession limit is 10. Verify current rules with CDFW before fishing.

white_seabass.notes: Verify current size and bag limits with CDFW; rules may vary by region.

yellowtail.notes: Verify current bag limits and any area restrictions with CDFW.

kelp_bass.notes: Combined bass bag limit (kelp, sand, barred sand) may apply. Verify with CDFW.

sand_bass.notes: Combined bass bag limit (kelp, sand, barred sand) may apply. Verify with CDFW.

lingcod.season: Seasonal — check CDFW for current open dates
lingcod.notes: Season dates and bag limits vary by area (north vs. south). Verify before fishing.

corbina.notes: No state-regulated minimum size or bag limit. Hook and line only. Verify with CDFW.

cabezon.notes: Season and bag limits vary by CDFW management area. Verify current rules.

pacific_barracuda.notes: Single barbless hooks required. 28 in TL minimum statewide.

pacific_halibut.season: Varies by zone; generally open year-round south of Pt. Conception
pacific_halibut.notes: Check CDFW for area-specific rules; northern zones may have different seasons.

chinook_salmon.season: Set annually; varies by zone and river system
chinook_salmon.notes: Season dates set by CDFW and PFMC each year. ALWAYS verify before fishing — rules change frequently.

coho_salmon.notes: Coho salmon are protected in many CA waters. Verify current rules before fishing.

striped_bass.season: Open year-round in ocean and SF Bay
striped_bass.notes: Bag limit is 2 in tidal waters. Verify for Delta rules which differ.

rockfish_general.season: Varies by zone and depth; consult CDFW for closures
rockfish_general.notes: Rockfish rules are complex with depth/area restrictions. Verify current open areas before fishing.

black_rockfish.bag_limit: Included in 10-fish aggregate rockfish bag limit
black_rockfish.season: Varies by management area; check CDFW depth restrictions
black_rockfish.notes: CA rockfish rules are complex with Rockfish Conservation Areas. Verify open zones before fishing.

yelloweye_rockfish.bag_limit: 1 per day within aggregate; some areas CLOSED to harvest
yelloweye_rockfish.season: Varies; many areas prohibit retention due to rebuilding plan
yelloweye_rockfish.notes: Yelloweye rockfish are a rebuilding species. Retention is prohibited in many areas. Verify current rules — this is a high-compliance-risk species.

petrale_sole.notes: Part of the CA flatfish aggregate limit. Verify with CDFW.

pacific_sanddab.notes: One of the best eating fish in California; minimal regulation. Verify CDFW.

steelhead.bag_limit: 0 on most rivers (catch and release only)
steelhead.season: Varies by river; typically Nov-Mar in coastal rivers
steelhead.notes: Most California steelhead rivers are catch-and-release only for wild fish. Hatchery fish (clipped) may be retained where allowed. Verify CDFW rules by river.

california_spiny_lobster.notes: Hoop nets and hand-picking only (no traps for recreational). Minimum size is measured from rear of eye socket to rear of carapace. Verify CDFW season dates.

bocaccio.bag_limit: Included in 10-fish aggregate rockfish bag limit
bocaccio.season: Varies by area; check Rockfish Conservation Areas and depth restrictions
bocaccio.notes: Bocaccio is a rebuilding species. Retention rules vary by zone and year. Verify current rules before keeping any.

canary_rockfish.bag_limit: 1 per day within aggregate in some areas; prohibited in others
canary_rockfish.season: Check current year rules — often prohibited from retention
canary_rockfish.notes: Canary rockfish is a rebuilding species. Retention is prohibited in many zones. HIGH compliance risk — verify before keeping.

widow_rockfish.season: Open most of year; check depth restrictions
widow_rockfish.notes: Verify current open areas before fishing.

pacific_ocean_perch.season: Open most of year; check depth restrictions

thornyheads.notes: Shortspine and longspine thornyheads have a combined 10-fish limit in most Pacific Coast regulations.

pacific_spiny_dogfish.notes: No California bag or size limit for spiny dogfish.

sevengill_shark.notes: No specific California regulations for sevengill sharks. Popular in SF Bay; most anglers practice catch and release.

tope_shark.notes: Tope (soupfin) sharks are unregulated for recreational anglers in California state waters.

dover_sole.notes: Part of the flatfish aggregate limit. Verify current state rules.

rex_sole.notes: Included in flatfish aggregate. Verify state rules.

surfperch_aggregate.min_size: Varies by species; most have no minimum size
surfperch_aggregate.notes: Surfperch (pile perch, rainbow seaperch, striped seaperch, pink seaperch, shiner perch, etc.) fall under a 20-fish daily bag aggregate in most Pacific states. Verify current state rules.

spotted_sand_bass.bag_limit: 10 per day (sand bass aggregate with barred sand bass)
spotted_sand_bass.season: Closed Mar 1 – Jun 15 (spawning closure in some years)
spotted_sand_bass.notes: Spotted and barred sand bass share a 10-fish aggregate limit. Spawning closure applies in Southern California waters; verify current CDFW rules.

chilipepper_rockfish.season: Open most of year; check depth restrictions
chilipepper_rockfish.notes: Part of the rockfish complex. Verify current area/depth rules.

shortbelly_rockfish.notes: No specific limit; part of rockfish aggregate.

greenstriped_rockfish.notes: Part of rockfish aggregate. Verify current rules.

pacific_sand_dab.notes: Pacific sand dabs have no bag or size limit in most Pacific states. They are among the most lightly regulated flatfish species.

speckled_sand_dab.notes: No specific regulations; verify current state rules.

butter_sole.bag_limit: 10 per day (flatfish aggregate in some areas)
butter_sole.notes: Part of the general flatfish group. Verify current state flatfish aggregate rules.

sand_sole.bag_limit: 10 per day (flatfish aggregate in some areas)
sand_sole.notes: Part of the general flatfish group. Verify current state flatfish aggregate rules.

white_croaker.notes: No size limit for white croaker. Check local consumption advisories — some Southern California harbors have fish consumption warnings due to sediment contamination.

pacific_mackerel.notes: No state size or bag limit for Pacific mackerel. Abundance varies with ocean conditions.

jack_mackerel_pacific.notes: No specific regulations for Pacific jack mackerel in most states.

surf_smelt.notes: Check CDFW current rules for surf smelt dip-netting at specific Northern California beaches.

barred_sand_bass.bag_limit: 10 per day (aggregate with spotted sand bass)
barred_sand_bass.season: Closed Mar 1 – Jun 15 (spawning closure in many years)
barred_sand_bass.notes: Barred and spotted sand bass share a 10-fish aggregate limit. Spawning closure applies in Southern California. Verify current CDFW rules before fishing.

leopard_shark.notes: Leopard sharks are managed under California Leopard/Soupfin/Smoothhound complex. Verify current CDFW rules. Most anglers practice catch and release.

soupfin_shark.notes: Soupfin shark has no specific size limit but counts toward the general elasmobranch bag limit. Verify current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW rules.

gray_smoothhound.notes: Gray and brown smoothhounds share the general Pacific shark bag limit. No specific size limit. Verify current state rules.

brown_smoothhound.notes: Gray and brown smoothhounds share the general Pacific shark bag limit. No specific size limit. Verify current state rules.

pacific_electric_ray.notes: No specific regulations for Pacific electric ray. WARNING: they deliver a strong electric shock — never handle directly. Cut the leader to release.

pacific_tomcod.notes: No specific bag or size limit for Pacific tomcod in most Pacific states. Verify current state rules.

eulachon.notes: Eulachon are listed as a Species of Concern; some California populations have limited or no open seasons. Check current CDFW rules.

black_croaker.notes: No specific size limit for black croaker. Check local consumption advisories for Southern California bays.

white_seaperch.notes: White seaperch count toward the general surfperch aggregate bag limit. Verify current state rules.

pacific_whiting.notes: No specific recreational regulations for Pacific whiting. The commercial fishery is managed under PFMC. Check current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW rules.

blacksmith_pacific.notes: Blacksmith are part of the general nearshore fish regulations in California. Verify current CDFW rules.

plainfin_midshipman.notes: No specific regulations for plainfin midshipman. Mild venom in dorsal spines — handle with care.

garibaldi.notes: Garibaldi are the California state marine fish and are FULLY PROTECTED. It is illegal to take, possess, or harm them. Violations are a misdemeanor and carry fines up to $1,000.

cowcod.season: Closed — Cowcod Conservation Areas (CCAs) restrict access
cowcod.notes: Cowcod retention is prohibited in California and in federal Cowcod Conservation Areas. Release immediately. Check CDFW and NMFS closure maps before deep-water rockfish fishing south of Point Conception.

yellowtail_rockfish.bag_limit: 10 per day (shelf rockfish aggregate in most areas)
yellowtail_rockfish.season: Check current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW season calendar — seasons and depths vary by area
yellowtail_rockfish.notes: Yellowtail rockfish count toward the general shelf rockfish daily bag limit. Verify current state rules and area-specific depth restrictions.

greenspotted_rockfish.notes: Counted in the general rockfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

sharpchin_rockfish.notes: Counted in the general rockfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

redbanded_rockfish.notes: Counted in the general rockfish aggregate. Verify current state rules.

coho_salmon_pacific.bag_limit: 2 per day in ocean (varies by area)
coho_salmon_pacific.season: Check CDFW ocean and river seasons carefully — coho are protected in most California rivers; ocean season typically July-October
coho_salmon_pacific.notes: Coho salmon regulations are extremely complex in California. Some river populations are listed as Threatened. Always verify current CDFW rules before fishing.

chum_salmon.season: Check CDFW — chum are rare in California
chum_salmon.notes: Chum salmon are rare south of Washington. Limited returns to some northern California rivers.

pink_salmon.season: Check CDFW — pinks rarely reach California
pink_salmon.notes: Pink salmon barely enter California. Mostly a Washington/Oregon species.

sockeye_salmon.season: Check CDFW — sockeye rare in California
sockeye_salmon.notes: Sockeye are rare in California. Primarily a PNW species.

dolly_varden.season: Check CDFW — Dolly Varden are rare in California
dolly_varden.notes: Dolly Varden are rare in California; primarily found in far northern CA streams.

wahoo_pacific.min_size: None for mahi; varies for billfish
wahoo_pacific.bag_limit: 10 per day mahi; billfish: check NOAA HMS rules
wahoo_pacific.notes: Pacific billfish and large pelagics require federal NOAA HMS permits for some species. Striped marlin and sailfish should be released. Verify current CDFW and NOAA HMS rules.

mahi_mahi_pacific.min_size: None for mahi; varies for billfish
mahi_mahi_pacific.bag_limit: 10 per day mahi; billfish: check NOAA HMS rules
mahi_mahi_pacific.notes: Pacific billfish and large pelagics require federal NOAA HMS permits for some species. Striped marlin and sailfish should be released. Verify current CDFW and NOAA HMS rules.

striped_marlin.min_size: None for mahi; varies for billfish
striped_marlin.bag_limit: 10 per day mahi; billfish: check NOAA HMS rules
striped_marlin.notes: Pacific billfish and large pelagics require federal NOAA HMS permits for some species. Striped marlin and sailfish should be released. Verify current CDFW and NOAA HMS rules.

pacific_sailfish.min_size: None for mahi; varies for billfish
pacific_sailfish.bag_limit: 10 per day mahi; billfish: check NOAA HMS rules
pacific_sailfish.notes: Pacific billfish and large pelagics require federal NOAA HMS permits for some species. Striped marlin and sailfish should be released. Verify current CDFW and NOAA HMS rules.

yellowfin_tuna_pacific.notes: Pacific yellowfin tuna are regulated under NOAA HMS. Verify current state and federal bag limits.

pacific_bluefin_tuna.bag_limit: 3 per day (ICCAT/NOAA western Atlantic and Pacific bluefin quota may apply)
pacific_bluefin_tuna.season: Open year-round offshore; quota may close season early
pacific_bluefin_tuna.notes: Pacific bluefin tuna are under international quota management (IATTC). Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing — seasons may be shortened based on quota.

green_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

spotted_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

chain_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

california_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

darkblotched_rockfish.season: Check current CDFW depth/area closures; darkblotched is a rebuilding stock
darkblotched_rockfish.notes: Darkblotched rockfish count toward the general shelf rockfish bag limit. Some areas have depth restrictions. Verify current CDFW and PFMC rules.

pacific_grenadier.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

walleye_pollock.notes: No specific recreational regulations. Verify current state rules.

spiny_dogfish_pacific.notes: Pacific spiny dogfish have no bag or size limit. Handle with care — they have a venomous dorsal spine.

pacific_angel_shark.notes: Pacific angel sharks are fully protected in California. Release immediately if caught. Federal listing as Endangered Species applies.

bat_ray_pacific.notes: Bat ray bag limit is 2 per day in California. They have a venomous tail spine — handle carefully.

banded_guitarfish.notes: No specific regulations for banded guitarfish. Verify current state rules.

longbill_spearfish.notes: Spearfish are covered by NOAA HMS regulations. Verify current rules; most are released.

blackfin_tuna.notes: Blackfin tuna have no federal bag or size limit. Check state rules; generally no restriction for recreational anglers.

blue_runner.notes: No state regulations for blue runner in most Gulf and SE states; excellent live bait species.

rock_hind_grouper.notes: Included in the grouper complex aggregate limit. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

yellowmouth_grouper.notes: Included in the grouper complex aggregate limit. Verify current NOAA and state rules.

swordfish.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS recreational permit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules and possession limits. Strong conservation ethic — most are released.

bigeye_tuna.season: Open year-round; Atlantic bigeye quota applies
bigeye_tuna.notes: Bigeye tuna are under ICCAT quota management. Verify current NOAA HMS possession limits. Charter captains must check current quota availability.

atlantic_menhaden.notes: No recreational bag or size limit for menhaden in most Atlantic states. Commercial harvest is managed by ASMFC. Cast-netting for live bait is widely practiced.

cero_mackerel.notes: Cero mackerel rules are similar to Spanish mackerel in most states. Verify current FL FWC and NC/SC rules.

spotted_eagle_ray.notes: No specific bag limit but rays are considered a species of concern. Practice catch and release; they have venomous tail spines — handle with great care.

cownose_ray.notes: No state regulations for cownose ray in most Mid-Atlantic states. Some states run bow-fishing and bowfishing tournaments during spring/fall runs.

atlantic_guitarfish.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic guitarfish. Handle with care — they have small dorsal spines.

french_grunt.notes: Grunts fall under a 100-fish aggregate bag limit in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

cottonwick_grunt.notes: Grunts fall under a 100-fish aggregate bag limit in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

caesar_grunt.notes: Grunts fall under a 100-fish aggregate bag limit in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

bigeye_scad_atlantic.notes: No specific regulations for scad species. Commonly used as live bait.

round_scad.notes: No specific regulations for scad species. Commonly used as live bait.

gizzard_shad.notes: No recreational regulations for gizzard shad in most states. Cast-netting permitted as bait collection.

striped_burrfish.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

sharpnose_puffer.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

balloonfish.notes: No specific regulations. Most anglers release incidental catches. Note: pufferfish can be toxic if improperly cleaned.

atlantic_tripletail.notes: Florida has a 15 in minimum and 2-fish bag limit for tripletail. Verify current FL FWC rules.

goldface_tilefish.notes: Goldface and blackline tilefish are part of the Gulf/Atlantic deepwater tilefish complex. Verify current NOAA/GULF COUNCIL regulations.

blackline_tilefish.notes: Goldface and blackline tilefish are part of the Gulf/Atlantic deepwater tilefish complex. Verify current NOAA/GULF COUNCIL regulations.

hogfish_atlantic.min_size: 12 in TL in Gulf; 14 in TL in Atlantic
hogfish_atlantic.season: Gulf: open year-round. Atlantic: check FL FWC for current season.
hogfish_atlantic.notes: Hogfish are heavily regulated in Florida. Atlantic hogfish have seasonal closures. Verify current FL FWC rules as they change frequently.

spanish_hogfish.bag_limit: No specific limit (counted in wrasse/reef fish aggregate)
spanish_hogfish.notes: Spanish hogfish are not specifically regulated in most states; may count toward a general reef fish bag limit.

atlantic_spanish_mackerel.bag_limit: 15 per person per day in most states
atlantic_spanish_mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel regulations are similar across SE/Mid-Atlantic states. FL has a 12-inch minimum. Verify current state rules.

almaco_jack.bag_limit: No specific bag limit (part of amberjack complex in some states)
almaco_jack.notes: Almaco jack are often grouped under the amberjack complex in state and federal regulations. Verify current rules with FL FWC or relevant state agency.

banded_rudderfish.notes: No specific regulations for banded rudderfish in most states. Verify current rules.

bar_jack.notes: No specific regulations for bar jack in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

african_pompano.bag_limit: 10 per person per day (jack complex in most states)
african_pompano.notes: African pompano may be counted under the general jack aggregate limit. Verify current state rules. Excellent eating — worth keeping a few.

blue_tang_atlantic.notes: Most ornamental reef fish have no specific recreational bag limit in Florida but are subject to the general reef fish regulations. Some species may be prohibited from collection for commercial aquarium trade without permits. Verify current FL FWC rules.

ocean_surgeon.notes: Most ornamental reef fish have no specific recreational bag limit in Florida but are subject to the general reef fish regulations. Some species may be prohibited from collection for commercial aquarium trade without permits. Verify current FL FWC rules.

doctorfish.notes: Most ornamental reef fish have no specific recreational bag limit in Florida but are subject to the general reef fish regulations. Some species may be prohibited from collection for commercial aquarium trade without permits. Verify current FL FWC rules.

clown_wrasse.notes: Most ornamental reef fish have no specific recreational bag limit in Florida but are subject to the general reef fish regulations. Some species may be prohibited from collection for commercial aquarium trade without permits. Verify current FL FWC rules.

yellowhead_wrasse.notes: Most ornamental reef fish have no specific recreational bag limit in Florida but are subject to the general reef fish regulations. Some species may be prohibited from collection for commercial aquarium trade without permits. Verify current FL FWC rules.

creole_wrasse.notes: Most ornamental reef fish have no specific recreational bag limit in Florida but are subject to the general reef fish regulations. Some species may be prohibited from collection for commercial aquarium trade without permits. Verify current FL FWC rules.

longtail_tuna.min_size: 27 in curved fork length (grouped with large tuna)
longtail_tuna.notes: Longtail tuna are grouped under NOAA HMS tuna regulations. Verify current federal and state rules.

three_line_grunt.notes: No specific state regulations. Part of general reef fish rules in Florida.

belted_sandfish.notes: No specific state regulations. Part of general reef fish rules in Florida.

yelloweye_snapper.notes: Grouped under the snapper complex in most Gulf and SE states. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

wenchman_snapper.notes: Grouped under the snapper complex in most Gulf and SE states. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

permit_offshore.notes: Florida permits have a 100-fish daily bag limit and 11-inch minimum; offshore permit on wrecks count the same. Verify current FL FWC rules.

nassau_grouper.notes: Nassau grouper are critically endangered and fully protected under federal and Florida law. Immediate release required. Violations carry significant federal penalties.

black_grouper.min_size: 24 in TL in Atlantic; 20 in TL in Gulf (verify current rules)
black_grouper.notes: Black grouper regulations are complex and change frequently. They count toward the grouper complex limit. Always verify current FL FWC and NOAA rules before targeting.

goliath_grouper.notes: Goliath grouper are fully protected in US waters. Do not target; release immediately if caught without removing from water. Violations carry federal penalties.

gulf_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
gulf_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

northern_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
northern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

southern_kingfish.bag_limit: No recreational limit in most states
southern_kingfish.notes: No specific bag or size limit for sea mullet/kingfish in most Atlantic and Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

atlantic_threadfin.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic threadfin. Primarily used as live bait; cast-netting is the standard harvest method.

tripletail_gulf.notes: Gulf tripletail have a 15-inch minimum and 2-fish bag limit in most Gulf states. Verify current GMFMC and state rules.

wahoo_atlantic.bag_limit: 2 per person per day in most states
wahoo_atlantic.notes: Wahoo regulations vary by state. Most SE/Gulf states have a 2-fish bag limit. Verify current state rules.

green_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

spotted_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

chain_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

california_moray.notes: No specific regulations for moray eels. Handle with extreme caution — they have sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Cut the leader rather than attempting to handle.

puddingwife_wrasse.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

silver_perch_atlantic.notes: No specific regulations. Verify current state rules.

black_sea_bass_atlantic.season: Open year-round in most SE states
black_sea_bass_atlantic.notes: Verify current SAFMC and state rules for black sea bass.

sheepshead_atlantic.notes: Florida sheepshead have a 12-inch minimum and 15-fish bag limit. Verify current FL FWC rules.

dog_snapper.notes: Part of the snapper complex in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

mahogany_snapper.notes: Part of the snapper complex in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

glasseye_snapper.notes: Part of the snapper complex in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

graysby.notes: Part of the Southeast grouper complex. Verify current FL FWC and NOAA rules.

coney_grouper.notes: Part of the Southeast grouper complex. Verify current FL FWC and NOAA rules.

gray_tilefish.notes: Part of the Gulf/SE tilefish complex. Verify current GMFMC/SAFMC rules.

atlantic_blacktip_shark.notes: Shark regulations require a federal HMS Angling Permit for non-Atlantic coastal state recreational fishing. Verify current NOAA HMS rules for blacktip shark.

spinner_shark.notes: Spinner sharks are managed under NOAA HMS shark rules. Verify current regulations.

caribbean_reef_shark.notes: Managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current federal shark regulations. Practice catch-and-release.

lemon_shark.notes: Lemon sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Verify current regulations.

sand_tiger_shark.season: Check current state and federal rules
sand_tiger_shark.notes: Sand tiger sharks are protected in some states (NC, VA). Release immediately. Check current NOAA HMS and state rules.

skipjack_tuna_atlantic.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for skipjack tuna in most Atlantic states. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

cobia_juvenile.min_size: Same as adult cobia — 33 in (Atlantic) or 36 in (Gulf) FL
cobia_juvenile.bag_limit: 1 per person per day (Atlantic); 2 per person Gulf
cobia_juvenile.notes: Cobia regulations apply regardless of size. Atlantic: 33 in minimum, 1 fish per day. Gulf: 36 in minimum, 2 fish per day. Verify current state rules.

redfish_juvenile.bag_limit: 1 per person per day in most states; FL Gulf 2 per day
redfish_juvenile.notes: Redfish (red drum) slot limits apply — fish outside the slot must be released. Florida Gulf: 18-27 in slot, 2 fish/day. Verify current state slot limits carefully.

tarpon_juvenile.min_size: No minimum for catch-and-release; harvesting requires special permit in FL
tarpon_juvenile.bag_limit: Catch-and-release only (FL requires tarpon tag to harvest)
tarpon_juvenile.notes: Tarpon are primarily catch-and-release. Florida requires a $50 tarpon tag to harvest a tarpon. Most anglers release all tarpon.

snook_inshore.season: Atlantic coast: Jun 1-Aug 31 and Dec 1-Feb 28 closed. Gulf: closed Jun-Aug and Dec-Feb. Check FL FWC for current dates.
snook_inshore.notes: Snook have season closures and a 1-fish bag limit in Florida. Snook require a special snook permit (included in FL recreational license). Verify current FL FWC rules carefully — snook regulations are complex.

bonefish_flats.notes: Bonefish are catch-and-release only in Florida. Handle gently, use wet hands, and release immediately. Do not lift by jaw.

permit_flats.notes: Permit have a 22-inch minimum and 2-fish bag limit in Florida. Handle gently and release large fish. Verify current FL FWC rules.

tarpon_adult.min_size: N/A for catch-and-release; harvest requires special tag
tarpon_adult.bag_limit: Catch-and-release only without tag; 1 fish with special tarpon tag ($50)
tarpon_adult.notes: Tarpon require a special tarpon tag to harvest in Florida. Almost all recreational tarpon are released. Handle gently, minimize air exposure, and revive before releasing.

ladyfish.notes: No specific regulations for ladyfish in Florida.

spotted_seatrout_gulf.notes: Spotted seatrout regulations vary by region within Florida — Gulf coast has different rules than Atlantic coast. Verify current FL FWC rules.

sheepshead_gulf.notes: Same as sheepshead Atlantic — verify current FL FWC rules.

red_snapper_gulf.season: Short federal season — check current NOAA season announcement (typically July-August, varies annually)
red_snapper_gulf.notes: Gulf red snapper have a 16-inch minimum and 2-fish bag limit. The season is VERY SHORT and changes each year. Check NOAA Fisheries for current season dates before planning a trip. State waters may have different rules.

sailfish_atlantic.notes: Sailfish primarily caught off SE Florida coast. HMS Angling Permit required for harvest. Almost always released.

wahoo_east.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for wahoo in Gulf/SE states. Verify current state rules.

dolphinfish_mahi_school.notes: Verify current state rules for mahi-mahi.

red_drum_adult.min_size: Typically over the slot (27 in and above) — must be RELEASED in most states
red_drum_adult.bag_limit: 0 (must release oversized fish above slot in most states)
red_drum_adult.notes: Oversized red drum above the slot limit (typically 27 in) must be released in most states. Slot limits vary by state — verify current state rules. Oversized fish are prime breeders and critical to the population.

cobia_adult.min_size: 33 in (Atlantic FL) / 36 in (Gulf FL) fork length
cobia_adult.bag_limit: 1 per person per day (Atlantic); 2 per person (Gulf)
cobia_adult.notes: Cobia minimum and bag limits differ on Atlantic and Gulf coasts of Florida. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

lesser_amberjack.notes: Part of the amberjack complex. Verify current state rules.

ballyhoo.notes: No specific regulations for ballyhoo. Primarily used as bait.

gray_snapper.notes: Gray snapper (mangrove snapper) count toward the snapper aggregate limit in Florida. Verify current FL FWC rules.

tiger_grouper.notes: Tiger grouper count toward the Southeast grouper complex. Verify current FL FWC rules.

yellowtail_snapper.notes: Yellowtail snapper count toward the Florida snapper aggregate. Verify current FL FWC rules.

lane_snapper.notes: Lane snapper count toward the FL snapper aggregate. Verify current FL FWC rules.

bluestriped_grunt.notes: Part of the Florida grunt aggregate. Verify current FL FWC rules.

hardhead_catfish.notes: No specific regulations for hardhead catfish. Considered a nuisance in most areas. Has venomous spines — handle with extreme care.

gafftopsail_catfish.notes: No specific regulations for gafftopsail catfish. Has venomous spines; handle carefully. Better eating than hardhead catfish.

atlantic_torpedo_ray.notes: Atlantic torpedo rays can deliver powerful electric shocks (up to 220 volts) — DO NOT TOUCH. Cut the leader and release at the waterline. No regulations but no reason to retain them.

atlantic_spadefish.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic spadefish. Verify current state rules.

blue_tang.notes: No specific regulations for blue tang. They are primarily herbivores and rarely targeted. Release immediately in most contexts.

ocean_surgeonfish.notes: No specific regulations. Handle with extreme caution — razor-sharp scalpel spine at tail base can inflict deep cuts. Release quickly.

great_barracuda.notes: No specific size or bag limit for great barracuda in most SE states. Ciguatera fish poisoning risk — most anglers release large barracuda. Use wire leader.

florida_gar.notes: No specific regulations for Florida gar in most states.

alligator_gar.bag_limit: 1 per day in TX; no limit in some states
alligator_gar.season: Check current state season; TX requires a tag
alligator_gar.notes: Alligator gar regulations vary significantly by state. Texas requires a tag and has seasonal rules. Louisiana has no limit. Verify current state rules — alligator gar populations are a conservation concern in some areas.

spotted_gar.notes: No specific regulations for spotted gar in most states.

shortnose_gar.notes: No specific regulations for shortnose gar.

slippery_dick.bag_limit: No limit (part of reef fish complex)
slippery_dick.notes: No specific regulations for slippery dick wrasse.

spotted_drum.notes: No specific regulations. These are incidental catches. Verify current state rules.

jackknife_fish.notes: No specific regulations. These are incidental catches. Verify current state rules.

highhat.notes: No specific regulations. These are incidental catches. Verify current state rules.

cubbyu.notes: No specific regulations. These are incidental catches. Verify current state rules.

reef_squirrelfish.notes: No specific regulations for squirrelfish. Verify current state rules.

longspine_squirrelfish.notes: No specific regulations for squirrelfish. Verify current state rules.

tilefish_blueline.notes: Blueline tilefish count toward the Southeast tilefish complex (7-fish limit). Verify current FL FWC and NOAA rules.

swordfish_atlantic.notes: Swordfish require a federal HMS Angling Permit. 47-inch LJFL minimum, 1 fish per person per day. NOAA Observer Program may apply. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

wahoo_gulf.notes: No specific bag limit for wahoo in Gulf states. Verify current state rules.

opah_atlantic.notes: No specific recreational regulations for Atlantic opah. Verify current state and NOAA HMS rules.

crevalle_jack_adult.notes: No specific size or bag limit for crevalle jack in most states. Verify current state rules.

horse_eye_jack.notes: No specific regulations. Note ciguatera risk in large fish. Verify current state rules.

bigeye_scad.notes: No specific regulations for bigeye scad. Primarily used as live bait.

red_porgy.notes: Part of the Southeast porgy complex. Verify current SAFMC and state rules.

jolthead_porgy.notes: Part of the Southeast porgy complex. Verify current SAFMC and state rules.

whitebone_porgy.notes: Part of the Southeast porgy complex. Verify current SAFMC and state rules.

knobbed_porgy.notes: Part of the Southeast porgy complex. Verify current SAFMC and state rules.

saucereye_porgy.notes: Part of the Southeast porgy complex. Verify current SAFMC and state rules.

banded_butterflyfish.notes: No specific regulations. These are release fish — please return to reef.

reef_butterflyfish.notes: No specific regulations. These are release fish — please return to reef.

neon_goby.notes: Cleaning gobies are not a hook-and-line target. Marine ecosystem role as cleaners — observe but do not target.

cleaning_goby.notes: Cleaning gobies are not a hook-and-line target. Marine ecosystem role as cleaners — observe but do not target.

sharknose_goby.notes: Cleaning gobies are not a hook-and-line target. Marine ecosystem role as cleaners — observe but do not target.

spotted_goatfish.notes: No specific regulations for goatfish. Verify current state rules.

yellow_goatfish.notes: No specific regulations for goatfish. Verify current state rules.

red_goatfish.notes: No specific regulations for goatfish. Verify current state rules.

bigeye_reef.notes: No specific regulations for bigeyes. Nocturnal reef fish, rarely targeted.

sailors_choice.notes: Part of the Florida/SE grunt complex. Verify current state rules.

latin_grunt.notes: Part of the Florida/SE grunt complex. Verify current state rules.

sailor_grunt.notes: Part of the Florida/SE grunt complex. Verify current state rules.

tomtate_grunt.notes: Part of the Florida/SE grunt complex. Verify current state rules.

porcupinefish.notes: CAUTION: Porcupinefish contain tetrodotoxin — do not eat. Handle carefully and release quickly.

orangespotted_filefish.notes: No specific regulations for orangespotted filefish. Release recommended.

smooth_trunkfish.notes: Smooth trunkfish secrete pahutoxin when stressed — do not mix with other fish in a livewell. Release recommended.

scrawled_filefish.notes: No specific regulations for scrawled filefish. Edible once rough skin removed — most are released.

great_hammerhead.notes: Great hammerhead sharks are PROHIBITED in the Atlantic and Gulf under federal HMS regulations. Release immediately. Critically Endangered — minimize handling, use dehooking tools in the water.

bonnethead_shark.notes: Bonnethead sharks managed under NOAA HMS. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit from a vessel. 1-fish vessel limit. Mostly released.

inshore_shark.notes: Inshore shark fishing requires a federal HMS Angling Permit. Most small coastal sharks have a 1-fish vessel daily limit. Verify current NOAA HMS rules before fishing.

nurse_shark_juvenile.notes: Same regulations as adult nurse shark. Release recommended.

atlantic_sharpnose_shark_juvenile.notes: Same HMS regulations as adult sharpnose shark. Verify current NOAA HMS rules.

spanish_mackerel_atlantic.notes: Spanish mackerel: 14-inch FL minimum on Atlantic coast, 12-inch Gulf. 15-fish daily bag limit in most states. Verify current ASMFC and GMFMC rules.

king_mackerel_small.notes: King mackerel have a 24-inch minimum and 3-fish bag limit in most states. Gulf regulations may differ. Verify current SAFMC, GMFMC and state rules.

little_tunny_small.notes: No specific bag limit for little tunny (false albacore). Same as adult little tunny. Not recommended for eating by most anglers.

bonito_atlantic.notes: No specific regulations for Atlantic bonito. Verify current state rules.

florida_pompano_juvenile.min_size: 11 in (FL) — must be released if under minimum
florida_pompano_juvenile.bag_limit: 6 per day when at or above minimum size
florida_pompano_juvenile.notes: Juvenile pompano under the minimum size must be released. Same regulations as adult Florida pompano.

permit_small.min_size: 22 in fork length (same as flats permit)
permit_small.bag_limit: 2 per person per day (same as flats permit)
permit_small.notes: Same regulations as permit (flats). Verify current state rules.

permit_large.notes: Same permit regulations apply at any size. Verify current FL FWC and state rules.

snook_common.season: Atlantic: Mar 1-May 31, Sep 1-Nov 30; Gulf: Mar 1-May 31, Sep 1-Nov 30 (closed Jun-Aug and Dec-Feb)
snook_common.notes: Special snook permit required. One fish per day within slot. Trophy fish (over max) must be released.

fat_snook.notes: Snook permit required. Species rarely reach legal size — catch and release.

swordspine_snook.notes: Snook permit required. Species rarely reach legal size — catch and release.

bonefish_gulf.notes: Catch-and-release only. Same rules as Atlantic bonefish. Handle in water, revive fully.

amberjack_lesser.notes: Gulf reef fish permit not required for lesser amberjack. Different from greater amberjack regulations.

stone_crab.notes: Only one claw per crab may be taken. Crab must be returned alive. Females must be released. No claws in closed season.

spiny_lobster_caribbean.season: Aug 6 - Mar 31; Mini-season last Wed-Thu in July (12/day)
spiny_lobster_caribbean.notes: No hooks, spears, or wire. Tickle stick and net only. Egg-bearing females must be released. Federal sanctuary rules apply in Keys.

menhaden_atlantic.notes: Not caught on hook and line. Used as bait and chum. Commercial harvest managed by ASMFC.

gulf_menhaden.notes: Used as bait. Commercial harvest managed separately.

gizzard_shad_tidal.notes: Cast net only — not caught on hook and line. Typically used as bait.

flounder_gulf.notes: Gulf and Atlantic coasts — same size limit.

cobia_near_pier.notes: Atlantic cobia managed by ASMFC. 1 fish per angler. Very popular spring sight-fishing target.

cobia_offshore.notes: Same size and bag limit as near-pier cobia.

atlantic_croaker_large.notes: Not regulated in most states. Some states have size or possession limits for commercial harvest. Check state rules.

blacktip_shark.notes: NOAA HMS Angling Permit required if targeting sharks. Catch-and-release encouraged. Never cut fins (federal shark finning ban).

atlantic_sharpnose_shark.notes: Small coastal shark — no minimum size. HMS Angling Permit required.

bull_shark_inshore.notes: NOAA HMS Angling Permit required to target sharks. Very heavy tackle required. Release strongly encouraged — bull sharks are apex predators with slow reproduction.

skipjack_tuna_shore.notes: Federal pelagic fish — no HMS permit needed for recreational hook-and-line. Dark flesh — best used as bait.

tilefish_sand.notes: Not managed separately from other tilefish in most SE states. Check state rules.

yellowfin_mojarra.notes: Not typically regulated — forage and bait species.

atlantic_spadefish_pier.notes: Not heavily regulated. Spadefish are excellent table fare — white, mild flesh.

sea_bream_pinfish.notes: Primarily used as live bait. Catch by cast net or tiny hook with shrimp.

mud_snapper.notes: Juvenile snapper in estuaries. Same regulations as the parent species (gray snapper, lane snapper) — check state rules.

grass_porgy.notes: Not separately regulated in most states.

sheepshead_porgy.notes: Not separately regulated — falls under general reef fish or porgy rules.

dwarf_sand_perch.notes: Too small to be targeted or regulated. Release if incidentally caught.

butter_hamlet.notes: Hamlet species are small reef fish not targeted by anglers. Incidental hook catches should be immediately released.

speckled_trout_sea_trout.notes: Emergency rules possible after cold kills.

speckled_trout_winter.notes: Emergency rules possible after cold kills.

tarpon_gulf_mexico.notes: FL: $50 tarpon tag required. Catch-and-release universal. Revive thoroughly before release.

snook_gulf.notes: Special snook permit required. Closed Jun-Aug and Dec-Feb on Gulf coast.

atlantic_sturgeon_catch_and_release.notes: ESA ENDANGERED. Illegal to target, possess, or harm. Release immediately. Report to NOAA: 1-800-853-1964.

goliath_grouper_encounter.notes: Illegal to harvest or possess. FL: cannot be removed from water without scientific permit.

bluefish_large.notes: ASMFC 3-fish bag limit. Use wire or heavy mono leader — razor teeth.

bluefish_snapper_blues.notes: Same 3-fish bag limit. Wire or heavy mono leader required.

red_snapper_gulf_large.notes: NOAA SERO annual season extremely short. State waters may differ. Barotrauma concern — use descender device.

sawfish_encounter.notes: If accidentally caught do NOT remove from water. Cut line close to mouth. Call FWC immediately.

manta_ray_encounter.notes: Cannot be targeted or harassed in US federal waters.

whale_shark_encounter.notes: Illegal to target or harm. Observe from 6 ft minimum distance. Do not ride or touch.

midnight_parrotfish.notes: Critical reef species. Not regulated but release is strongly encouraged.

pufferfish_northern.notes: SKIN IS TOXIC — do not eat skin. Properly cleaned northern puffer (sea squab) is edible and considered a delicacy.

atlantic_halfbeak.notes: Primarily used as offshore trolling bait (ballyhoo). No regulations.

common_snook_atlantic_fl.notes: Special snook permit required. Atlantic slot is 28-33 in (vs 28-32 on Gulf).

permit_atlantic.notes: Permit are catch-and-release in most tournament settings. Legal to keep with 11-inch minimum in FL (2/day).

pompano_atlantic.notes: One of the finest eating fish in Florida. Found in surf year-round.

cobia_early_season.notes: Same rules as regular cobia. Atlantic and Gulf cobia share 33-inch minimum. 1 fish per day.

southern_flounder_gigging.notes: Gigging regulations same as rod-and-reel limits. TX has restricted fall gigging season at pass mouths.

white_marlin.notes: White marlin are highly migratory and subject to NOAA HMS regulations. Requires federal HMS Angling Permit. Almost always released — they are an overfished stock. Report catches to the HMS recreational fishery observer program.

longfin_albacore.notes: No specific recreational bag limit for longfin albacore. Verify current NOAA HMS and state rules.

dolphinfish_mahi_school.notes: No specific bag limit for mahi-mahi in most states. Verify current state rules.
